sn37.3:1.1: _Mātugāma_ means “motherkind”. It is a word for women in Pali, but a problematic one. It does not seem to be in use outside of Buddhist texts, and perhaps was coined by the Buddha. Throughout the Pātimokkha it is used in apposition with _bhikkhu_, whereas _itthī_ is used with _purisa_. But there is no corresponding male form, so _bhikkhunī_ just takes _purisa_. So there is an asymmetry in usage. However, this does not obtain in the Suttas, as we see here _mātugāma_ used with _purisa_. The form is also puzzling, as it is masculine singular. It occurs in both singular and plural senses, as seen in this Sutta.
